In 1967 Anguillans rose against rule from St Kitts and expelled the St Kitts police on 30 May, now Anguilla Day. Britain had just joined the three islands as one associated state.

Led by Ronald Webster, the islanders voted to break away and for a time declared a republic. Talks failed, and in 1969 Britain sent paratroopers and police in Operation Sheepskin.

The outcome was what most Anguillans wanted: direct British rule instead of rule from Basseterre. The split from St Kitts and Nevis became formal in 1980, and Anguilla remains a British overseas territory.
